gate.rule: Pass only if all three hold for the two-part Poisson-Gamma model (Poisson frequency with exposure offset times Gamma severity on positive claims), fixed before results as the headline: (1) the 95% bootstrap interval on its pure premium Gini index against holdout losses has a lower bound above 0.25; (2) the 95% paired bootstrap interval on its Gini index minus that of the single compound Tweedie model has a lower bound above zero; (3) the actual loss ratio in the highest predicted risk decile is below 0.95.

ignoring_exposure_time.note: The model that ignores exposure time misprices short-duration policies because it treats raw claim count as the annualized rate.

loss_ratio_by_decile.note: Flat pricing heavily overcharges the safest segment and undercharges the riskiest segment, resulting in an unsustainable top-decile loss ratio.

one_model_for_frequency_and_size.note: Fitting a single compound Tweedie model conflates frequency drivers with severity drivers, reducing pricing discrimination and increasing pure premium error.

caveats: Everything is simulated. Driver risk parameters, vehicle values, and accident distributions are chosen by the author.
Exposure is simulated uniformly from 0.1 to 1.0 year without seasonality or cancellation correlation.
Individual claims are assumed independent and follow a Gamma distribution. Real severity often has heavy Pareto tails.
Features are limited to five synthetic variables without interaction terms or telematics data.
Intervals resample holdout policies. They do not cover model misspecification or a changing underlying environment.
